question: How long does delamination of lithium-ion battery electrodes in ethylene glycol take at 160 °C, and at the boiling point of ethylene glycol?
expect: about 6 s at 160 °C; around 2 s at the boiling point (198 °C) (p3.L136-138)
rendered:
The document "Sustainable Direct Recycling of Lithium-Ion Batteries via Solvent Recovery of Electrode Materials" contains the answer.

According to the document, delamination typically takes a couple of hours to be completed at room temperature (~20 °C), while less than 2 min are needed when increasing the reaction temperature to 100 °C. 

At 160 °C, the delamination takes around 6 seconds to fully peel off the cathode from the aluminum foil.

At the boiling point of ethylene glycol (198 °C), the delamination takes around 2 seconds to fully peel off the cathode from the aluminum foil.
